title: Sections of neutral algebraic gerbes are fppf presentations
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $V/S$ be a scheme, and let $a:\mathcal G\to V$ be a morphism from an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Use algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] and the fibred-groupoid and 2-fibre-product conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Suppose that $a$ is a gerbe: for every scheme $T\to V$, the groupoid of lifts to $\mathcal G$ has objects fppf locally on $T$, and any two such objects are isomorphic fppf locally [def-pc-fppf-site]. Let $x:V\to\mathcal G$ be a section, with a specified 2-isomorphism $ax\simeq\mathrm{id}_V$. Then $x$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Explicitly, for every scheme $T$ and object $y:T\to\mathcal G$, the projection $V\times_{x,\mathcal G,y}T\to T$ is a surjective flat locally finitely presented algebraic-space morphism. Flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No smoothness of the automorphism groups, Noetherian, separation or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: First regard $\mathcal G$ as an fppf stack: the etale-stack and smooth-atlas definition supplies precisely the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent]. Apply [lem-sfb-self-relation-quotient-embedding] to $x$. It gives the algebraic space $R=V\times_{\mathcal G}V$, its isomorphism-composition groupoid, and a fibrewise fully faithful map $i:[V/R]\to\mathcal G$ with $iq\simeq x$. An arrow $(v,w,\alpha)$ of $R(T)$ has $v=w$: applying $a$ to $\alpha:x(v)\simeq x(w)$ and using the specified $ax\simeq1_V$ gives equality in the discrete groupoid $V(T)$. Thus both projections $R\to V$ agree. Put $G=R$ over this common projection. Identity, composition and inverse are those of automorphisms of $x(v)$, so this is a group algebraic space over $V$. In particular the groupoid $(V,R)$ is exactly the trivial-action groupoid $(V,G)$, not an arbitrary action groupoid.

The quotient $[V/G]$ is an fppf stack by [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. For $y\in\mathcal G(T)$ put $v=ay:T\to V$. The two objects $x(v)$ and $y$ lie over the same $v$; the gerbe hypothesis gives an fppf covering $T_j\to T$ and isomorphisms $x(v)|_{T_j}\simeq y|_{T_j}$. Since $iq\simeq x$, these are local lifts through $i$. Both stacks are on the big fppf site, in the stipulated universes, and $i$ is fibrewise fully faithful by step 1. Consequently [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence] gives an equivalence $i:[V/G]\simeq\mathcal G$. This makes $[V/G]$ algebraic in the atlas definition: a quasi-inverse carries a smooth surjective scheme atlas of $\mathcal G$ to one of $[V/G]$; on scheme tests the unit and counit identify their fibre products and diagonals, preserving their algebraic-space representatives and smooth projections.

Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-classifying-stack-flatness] with $B=V$ and the group algebraic space $G$ of step 1. Its quotient is the fppf stackification already used in step 2, and that step proves it is algebraic. Hence $G\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Both source and target maps of $(V,G)$ are this very morphism, so both satisfy the hypotheses of the flat-groupoid quotient theorem; no smoothness of $G$ has been introduced.

By [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient], the object map $q:V\to[V/G]$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. For each $y:T\to\mathcal G$, choose its image $z:T\to[V/G]$ under a quasi-inverse of $i$. The unit, counit and $iq\simeq x$ identify $V\times_{[V/G]}T$ with $V\times_{\mathcal G}T$ over $T$: on test schemes they send a pair and its isomorphism to its image under $i$, with inverse induced by the quasi-inverse. Thus the latter projection has exactly the four properties of the former. As $T,y$ were arbitrary, this proves all assertions about $x$ and the explicit algebraic-space base changes.
